---
title: "Pilot Status"

This page is a public status snapshot of the Sacrificial Debt manual pilot. The
canonical records remain the versioned files in the repository; this page
summarizes what those records currently make visible.

::: {.callout-warning}
The pilot has not produced findings or released claims. Reviewed calibration
records are methodological evidence for testing the workflow, not proof of a
Sacrificial Debt mechanism.
:::

## What Exists

The pilot has a bounded Germany-first source plan, a locked manual codebook, a
provenance model, segmentation fixtures, and one real-source calibration chain.

The calibration chain uses Jacob Segall's 1922 statistical study of German
Jewish soldiers. It is treated as Tier 2 counterevidence/response material for
the Judenzaehlung source family. Its current role is to test whether documented
German Jewish war participation should qualify or rival claims that German Jews
failed to provide proportional military contribution.

The calibration packet is project-owner reviewed for methodological fit. It is
not expert-adjudicated, not a released finding, and not a strong Sacrificial
Debt annotation.

## What Remains Provisional

The pilot still needs:

- more rights-reviewed source captures;
- historical full page or document OCR/transcription captures where rights permit;
- additional readable rendered evidence packet pages as new packets are created;
- additional manually reviewed propositions across source families;
- reliability and adjudication rules for multiple coders;
- explicit evidence chains before any research claim is promoted.

Future packet expansion should be tracked with new bounded issues when more
canonical packet records exist.

## Not Yet Evidence

The following are not claim-ready evidence:

- Tier 3 source leads;
- synthetic segmentation fixtures;
- metadata-only source records;
- unreviewed source excerpts;
- observation-only annotations without interpretation;
- single-source calibration records;
- rhetoric treated as reception or policy causation without separate evidence.

No pilot record currently authorizes a public claim that Sacrificial Debt
explains Germany, the Holocaust, Judenzaehlung, Nazi policy, or any comparison
case.

## Falsification Burden

The workbench is designed to make weakening evidence visible. Negative evidence,
rival explanations, chronology problems, actor inconsistency, and absence
claims are first-class records.

Early claims would be weakened or blocked by evidence that:

- alleged non-contribution is contradicted by reliable contribution records;
- demonstrated service discharges or reclassifies the alleged debt;
- expected sacrificial-debt rhetoric is absent in a defined source universe;
- coercion occurs without debt, repayment, or equalization logic;
- debt rhetoric does not connect to reception, institution, or policy evidence;
- a rival explanation accounts for the same source pattern with less inference.

Absence claims require a documented search scope. A missing result from casual
search is not a valid absence claim.
